title: Locale Handoff Eval Playbook — CJK & RTL translation diffs
content:
Purpose:
This playbook describes a lightweight, repeatable evaluation and regression workflow for onboarding LLM checkpoints where multilingual behavior matters — specifically CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) and RTL (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian) locales, plus locale-aware formatting (dates, numbers, currency, addresses). The goal is to catch translation quality regressions, format corruption, and bidi/tokenization edge cases early in the model rollouts.

Scope and goals:
- Verify translation fidelity for short-to-mid form content (1–300 tokens) across 12 target locales.
- Detect hallucination and omission errors using targeted probes.
- Validate locale-sensitive formatting (dates, currencies, phone numbers, separators, address order).
- Surface CJK/RTL-specific tokenization and punctuation regressions (fullwidth vs halfwidth, Arabic diacritics, zero-width joiner/ non-joiner issues).
- Provide a diff-first regression report that can be consumed by release engineering and model owners.

Testset composition (recommended):
- Parallel segments: 1,500 aligned source-target pairs across 6 source languages -> 12 target locales. Include varied registers: UI strings, short emails, help text, product descriptions, and user-generated snippets.
- Formatting table: 300 synthetic rows covering date formats (YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, localized month names), currencies with symbols and codes, thousands/decimal separators, phone formats, postal address templates per locale.
- Bidi mix samples: 120 mixed LTR+RTL examples (English phrases embedded in Arabic/Hebrew context and vice versa), covering inline code, URLs, and quoted phrases.
- CJK quirks: 200 samples with punctuation normalization, kana/hangul spacing, Chinese punctuation (fullwidth commas, quotes), and classical/Hanja overlap cases.
- Hallucination probes: 150 crafted prompts that require factual preservation (dates, names, numeric facts) to detect content fabrication.

Design principles for cases:
- Minimal but high-signal: prefer shorter cases that isolate a single failure mode (e.g., currency symbol moving position).
- Variation coverage: include both naturally-occurring and synthetic variations to trigger tokenization artifacts.
- Deterministic seeds: synthetic generators use a small set of fixed seeds to keep the test corpus stable across runs.

Evaluation metrics and heuristics:
- Automatic metrics: chrF++ for CJK and low-resource pairs, BLEU (report with caution), and COMET (if available). Report per-locale metric slices.
- Locale-format metrics: exact-match rates for formatted fields (date normalized match; currency normalized match; phone canonicalization match).
- Bidi sanity checks: Unicode Bidi Algorithm conformance checks (visual rendering flags) and presence/absence of ZWJ/ZWNJ where expected.
- Tokenization drift: compare tokenizer-level token counts between baseline and candidate; flag > 30% relative change on samples that should be stable.
- Regression scoring: weighted score = 0.6 * COMET_normalized + 0.2 * formatting_exact_rate + 0.2 * bidi_sanity; for runs where COMET is not available, fall back to chrF++ with documented caveats.

Human review protocol:
- Triage failing cases using a small 3-reviewer panel (2 fluent annotators + 1 lead). Use three labels: OK, Minor issue (fluency/punctuation), Major issue (meaning changed/hallucinated).
- Consensus rule: majority label decides. If split three ways, escalate to lead for adjudication.
- Annotation guideline snippets: preserve entity order, numeric parity, and explicit date normalization rules. Provide concrete bad/good examples in the annotation UI.

Regression diff workflow (daily/nightly):
1) Baseline selection: choose the last production-pinned model (or specified commit) as baseline.
2) Run the full testset across baseline and candidate. Collect metrics, per-case diffs (token-level and normalized string diffs), and formatting flags.
3) Auto-prioritize failures by: (a) severity label estimate (hallucination > meaning drift > formatting), (b) per-case traffic weight (if we have telemetry), (c) locale criticality (customer-provided).
4) Produce a regression report with: top 20 high-impact failures, per-locale aggregated table, and example diffs with before/after texts and tokenizer traces.
5) Send to model owner and release channel with color-coded summary (red amber green) and attached CSV of all failing cases.

Actionable remediation steps (owner-facing):
- If hallucinations increase: limit sampling temperature, enable prefix-caching to preserve entities, and add targeted in-context exemplars for factual anchors.
- If tokenization drift occurs: lock tokenizers for rollout stage or apply tokenization-alignment transforms pre/post-inference.
- If formatting fails: add lightweight post-processing normalizers per-locale (dateparser, libphonenumber) and include failing examples in Optimize suggestions.

Example cases (extracts):
- CJK punctuation: Source: "会议, 明天 3/9" (expected zh-Hans: "会议，明天 3月9日") — check fullwidth comma and month name expansion.
- Arabic diacritics: Source: "سلمت الـمرفقات يوم 02-02-2026" (expected preserve diacritics/normalize spacing) — check for missing tashkeel and unexpected spacing.
- Mixed bidi code: Source: "Click here: https://example.com — انقر هنا" (expected maintain URL intact and correct visual ordering).
- Currency position: Source: "$ 1,234.50" (expected en-US -> "$1,234.50", fr-FR -> "1 234,50 €") — canonicalization rules must be applied.

Operational notes and tooling:
- Runner: use the onboarding harness at repo 'model-onboarding' (see linked GitHub PR). The harness should emit both raw outputs and normalized forms for metric calculation.
- Artifact retention: store per-run CSVs + tokenizer traces for 90 days in S3.
- Alerting: create a threshold monitor that triggers when weighted regression_score delta < -0.015 or when major-issue count increases by > 10 in a single run.

Reporting template (what the nightly brief must include):
- Header: baseline id, candidate id, run time, locale coverage summary.
- Top failures: list of top 20 with severity, sample, baseline, candidate, suggested remediation tag.
- Metric table: per-locale COMET/chrF/formatting-exact percentages + delta.
- Action items: owner assignments and ETA for fixes.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide whether COMET licensing is approved for nightly runs (Confluence-4821 tracking).
- Add telemetry weighting for samples based on production frequency (need SRE event mapping).
- Expand CJK test coverage for vertical text and variant glyphs (Han Traditional vs Simplified edge cases).

Appendix: quick checklist before signing off a candidate model:
- Run full testset and confirm no increase in major hallucinations.
- Confirm formatting exact-match >= baseline - 0.5% for each critical locale.
- Run bidi rendering sanity script on all mixed samples (no visual reordering regressions).
- Sanity-check tokenizer lengths on stable UI strings (delta < 30%).

Contact: Maya Chen (applied-ml) — ping in #eng-applied-ml for quick triage.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-03: initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2025-12-12: added bidi and tokenization checks (collaborator input).
- 2026-02-05: updated regression thresholds and reporting template for nightly runs.
